ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, it is known that \( I_1 = 5A \) and \( I_2 = 2A \). What is the current \( I_3 \)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the circuit is resistor R1, marked with a rightward current I1; the node after R1 splits into two upper and lower branches, the upper branch contains resistor R2 and is marked with a rightward branch current I2, and the lower branch contains resistor R4; the two branches recombine on the right side, then pass through resistor R3, and R3 is marked with a rightward current I3. Reasoning: R2 and R4 form a parallel two-terminal part, R1 is in series with the input terminal of this parallel part, and R3 is in series with the output terminal of this parallel part. Treating the R2/R4 parallel part as one overall two-terminal block, according to conservation of current, the total current entering this block equals the total current leaving this block. It is known that the total current in R1 is I1 = 5 A, so the total current I3 flowing out of the parallel block and through R3 is also equal to 5 A. I2 = 2 A is only the current in one of the branches, and is not needed for finding I3.

By conservation of current, the same total current that enters the block from R1 must leave through R3, so I3 = I1 = 5 A. I2 = 2 A is extra information not needed for this route.
